A factory produces \(m\) (\(i = 1, 2, \ldots, m\)) products, each of which requires processing on \(n\) (\(j = 1, 2, \ldots, n\)) workstations. Let \(a_{ij}\) be the amount of processing time that one unit of the \(i^{th}\) product requires on the \(j^{th}\) workstation. Let the revenue from selling one unit of the \(i^{th}\) product be \(r_i\) and \(h_i\) be the holding cost per unit per time period for the \(i^{th}\) product. The planning horizon consists of \(T\) (\(t = 1, 2, \ldots, T\)) time periods. The minimum demand that must be satisfied in time period \(t\) is \(d_{it}\), and the capacity of the \(j^{th}\) workstation in time period \(t\) is \(c_{jt}\). Consider the aggregate planning formulation below, with decision variables \(S_{it}\) (amount of product \(i\) sold in time period \(t\)), \(X_{it}\) (amount of product \(i\) manufactured in time period \(t\)) and \(I_{it}\) (amount of product \(i\) held in inventory at the end of time period \(t\)).
\[\max \sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{m}(r_iS_{it} - h_iI_{it})\]
subject to
\(S_{it} \ge d_{it}\quad \forall\ i, t\)
< capacity constraint >
< inventory balance constraint >
\(X_{it}, S_{it}, I_{it} \ge 0;\ I_{i0} = 0\)
The capacity constraints and inventory balance constraints for this formulation are
